newsitem.title: USA: Wal-Mart, Home Depot rally on strong earnings.
newsitem.headline: Wal-Mart, Home Depot rally on strong earnings.

text.p: Wal-Mart Stores Inc and Home Depot Tuesday charmed investors with strong fourth quarter earnings and bullish forecasts for 1997.
Shares of both retailers rallied on Tuesday and were among the most active issues on the New York Stock Exchange. Wal-Mart gained 1-1/4 to 25-7/8 and Home Depot jumped 2-1/4 to 54-1/2.

"Wal-Mart and Home Depot are the prinicipal stocks that are strong now and that are going to do much better. Consumer confidence is coming back and retailers are becoming a strong play," said Otto Grote, an analyst with Derby Securities.
Bentonville, Ark-based Wal-Mart posted fourth quarter earnings of $0.48 a share on net sales of $30.8 billion, compared to earnings of $0.41 a share on net sales of $27.6 billion last year.
Wal-Mart's earnings for the fourth quarter ended Jan 31 exceeding First Call analysts' estimates of $0.47 a share.
Wal-Mart, the nation's largest retailer, also said it was confident that it will post record sales and earnings in 1997.
Analysts said they expect Wal-Mart to benefit from continued cost controls and inventory reductions.
"Wal-Mart had a good quarter, in line with expectations," said Jeffrey Edelman, an analyst with Deutshe Morgan Grenfell. "And we'd of course expect them to have a record 1997."
The improvement in the retailer's Sam's Club division was the most encouraging sign, analysts said.
The Sam's Club unit posted fourth quarter operating profit of $274.0 million compared to $231.0 million last year.
Home Depot also pleased investors with solid earnings and a more optimistic growth target.
Home Depot posted fourth quarter earnings of $0.52 a share on net sales of $4.9 billion, up from earnings of $0.39 on net sales of $3.7 billion last year.
Analysts expected the Atlanta-based retailer to earn $0.49 a share, according to First Call.
"They've had a good year. And the outlook for next year is quite strong. They had some impressive results," said A.G. Edwards retail analyst Donald Spindel.

Home Depot attributed the strong results to the strength of its underlying business, and continuing consolidation in the retail home improvement industry, which combined to raise its 1996 market share to 14 percent from 12 percent in 1995.

Home Depot Inc also raised its target for earnings per share growth to 23-25 percent annually over the next two to three years. Previously, the company's long-term earnings per share growth target was 20-25 percent.
"They continue to gain market share. A lot of the growth they are seeing is from their aggressive new store expansion. But their existing stores continue to make a nice contribution," Spindel said.
Home Depot said it plans to spend $1.7 billion in 1997 to fund the addition of 111 new stores.
